title: How much sugar goes into each of the four bags?
description: A shopkeeper packs nine point five kilograms of sugar equally into four bags. The leftover One kilogram joins the Tenths, and the sharing goes on until nothing remains. Keeko's doubt is that the leftover One can be left out.
teaching_notes: One idea: a leftover One joins the Tenths before they are shared, so it is never dropped. Watch for students who share the Tenths alone and forget the One that remains.

source: A shopkeeper packs 9.5 kg of sugar equally into 4 bags. How much is in each bag?
video_script.why: The child can share a decimal with whole Ones but loses the leftover One when the Tenths are shared.
video_script.substitution: The leftover One joins the Tenths, and the sharing goes on place by place.
video_script.anchor: Nine point five kilograms of sugar, packed equally into four bags
video_script.wrong_answer: two point one two five kilograms
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko shares the Tenths alone and drops the leftover One, so each bag looks lighter than it should.
video_script.payoff_line: Each bag holds two point three seven five kilograms of sugar.

final_answer.spoken: two point three seven five kilograms

maths_rules: 1 One + 5 Tenths = 15 Tenths; 15 / 4 = 3 Tenths rem 3 Tenths
the slip: 5 Tenths shared alone gives 2.125, and 2.125 x 4 = 8.5, one kilogram short
video_script.design: The sugar bags stay on the board; the leftover One is carried into the Tenths and each leftover is regrouped one place lower.

marks.sack: the sack of nine point five kilograms appears above four empty bags

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is an example from your book about sharing sugar.
<bookmark mark='sack'/>A shopkeeper packs nine point five kilograms of sugar equally into four bags.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>How much sugar is in each bag?

beats.on_screen: the sack and the four bags stay on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: Ones and Tenths columns split by a decimal point; a leftover One block joining the Tenths blocks

marks.cols: the columns of Ones and Tenths sit on either side of the point
marks.join: a leftover One breaks into ten Tenths and joins the Tenths already there

narration: <bookmark mark='cols'/>The sugar is nine Ones and five Tenths, with the decimal point between them.
<bookmark mark='join'/>A leftover One breaks into ten Tenths, and these join the Tenths already there.

beats.on_screen: Given: 9 Ones + 5 Tenths of sugar, packed into 4 equal bags

marks.given: 9.5 kg and the four bags are written

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, nine Ones and five Tenths of sugar, to be packed into four equal bags.

beats.on_screen: To find: how much sugar each bag holds

marks.find: the share of one bag is outlined

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find how much sugar each of the four bags holds.

marks.s1b: two Ones go to each bag and one One remains

narration: <bookmark mark='s1a'/>Step one, share the Ones. We have nine Ones to pack into four bags.
<bookmark mark='s1b'/>Nine Ones divided by four gives two Ones for each bag, and one One remains.

beats.on_screen: decimal point placed; 1 One + 5 Tenths = 15 Tenths; 15 Tenths ÷ 4 = 3 Tenths each, 3 Tenths remain

marks.s2a: the decimal point is placed in the answer
marks.s2b: the leftover One breaks into ten Tenths and joins the five Tenths
marks.s2c: three Tenths go to each bag and three Tenths remain

narration: <bookmark mark='s2a'/>Step two, put the decimal point in the answer.
<bookmark mark='s2b'/>The leftover One becomes ten Tenths. With the five Tenths, that makes fifteen Tenths.
<bookmark mark='s2c'/>Fifteen Tenths divided by four gives three Tenths for each bag, and three Tenths remain.

beats.on_screen: 3 Tenths = 30 Hundredths; 30 Hundredths ÷ 4 = 7 Hundredths each, 2 Hundredths remain

marks.s3a: the three Tenths regroup into thirty Hundredths
marks.s3b: seven Hundredths go to each bag and two Hundredths remain

narration: <bookmark mark='s3a'/>Step three, regroup the three Tenths into thirty Hundredths.
<bookmark mark='s3b'/>Thirty Hundredths divided by four gives seven Hundredths for each bag, and two Hundredths remain.

beats.on_screen: 2 Hundredths = 20 Thousandths; 20 Thousandths ÷ 4 = 5 Thousandths each, nothing remains

marks.s4a: the two Hundredths regroup into twenty Thousandths
marks.s4b: five Thousandths go to each bag and nothing remains

narration: <bookmark mark='s4a'/>Step four, regroup the two Hundredths into twenty Thousandths.
<bookmark mark='s4b'/>Twenty Thousandths divided by four gives five Thousandths for each bag, and nothing remains.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>Each bag holds two point three seven five kilograms of sugar.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the four bags
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble shows 2.125 kg; four bags of 2.125 kg are weighed against 9.5 kg and fall one kilogram short; the bubble is crossed out

marks.fix: four bags of 2.125 kg are weighed against the sack and fall one kilogram short
marks.right: the leftover One is placed back with the Tenths

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks each bag holds two point one two five kilograms, because the five Tenths are shared alone.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>But four bags of that weight make only eight point five kilograms. That is one kilogram short of the sack.
<bookmark mark='right'/>The leftover One is never dropped. Break it into ten Tenths and share it with the Tenths.
